headline: Take-Two Interactive tumbles nearly 4.5% last night as oil slumps 5% and Labor pushes ahead with CGT changes tied to tax cuts.

portfolio.summary: A mostly quiet day on the ASX for your local holdings — CBA, VDHG, and VTS barely moved. The standout mover in your portfolio was Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) last night on the NASDAQ, dropping sharply ahead of the GTA 6 launch window. Oil's 5% plunge also weighed on your FUEL.AX energy ETF at today's close.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Fell nearly $10.53 last night to $227.55 USD. No single clear news catalyst — could be profit-taking or broader market jitters around the GTA 6 launch timeline and pre-order expectations. Worth watching.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Slipped $4.69 last night to $382.97 USD despite the new Gemini Omni announcement. Markets may be pausing to digest recent AI-related gains. Recent earnings were solid, so this looks like a routine pullback.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: Closed down at $8.78 today, dragged lower by a massive 5% crash in crude oil prices last night. OPEC also cut its global oil demand growth forecast for 2026, adding to the pressure on energy stocks.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: The one green light today — closed up at $92.66. Emerging markets got a small lift, possibly helped by a slightly firmer Aussie dollar and positive sentiment out of Asia.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: Nudged down slightly to $515.69 today, reflecting last night's mixed US session where the broader market was fairly flat.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Essentially flat last night at $418.57 USD — barely worth noting. AI and cloud growth story remains intact according to recent coverage.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 closed down 32 points (-0.37%) today at 8,660 — a mild retreat after recent gains. Last night's US session was more positive: the S&P 500 edged up 0.37% and the NASDAQ gained 0.19%. The big story in commodities is crude oil, which cratered nearly 5% last night to $91.79/barrel — that's a significant drop driven by OPEC cutting its demand growth forecast. Gold held steady near all-time highs at $4,526/oz. The Aussie dollar is sitting at 71.66 US cents, up slightly.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Closed down today — mild session, no major local catalysts.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session — modest gain, market holding up well.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Last night's session — slight gain despite weakness in GOOGL and TTWO.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Big drop last night — OPEC slashed its 2026 demand growth forecast, sending oil tumbling.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Barely moved — still sitting near record highs. Safe-haven demand holding.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Aussie dollar ticked up slightly — steady despite mixed RBA rate signals.

politics.summary: The big domestic story today is Labor pushing ahead with linking popular income tax cuts to capital gains tax (CGT) and negative gearing reforms — essentially saying 'you get the tax cuts if we can also change property investor rules.' The RBA rate path is also creating noise, with one expert breaking from the pack and calling for hikes.

stories.title: Labor ties $4,500 tax cuts to CGT and negative gearing changes
stories.why_it_matters: Labor wants to fund tax cuts worth around $4,500 for earners below $135,000 by making two changes that hurt property investors: raising the CGT (capital gains tax) discount — which reduces the tax you pay when selling an investment asset — from 50% down to 25%, and tightening negative gearing on existing properties (negative gearing lets investors claim losses on an investment property against their income). If you own investment properties or plan to sell assets, this directly affects your tax bill. Labor is ignoring calls from some quarters to pause the reform.

stories.title: Labor ignores calls for pause on CGT changes
stories.why_it_matters: Despite criticism from some economists and the property industry urging the government to slow down, Labor is pressing ahead with the CGT and negative gearing changes. The government is betting that the income tax cuts are popular enough to bring voters along, even if the property investor community pushes back hard.

stories.title: Expert breaks from consensus, demands RBA hike rates
stories.why_it_matters: While most economists and market traders expect the Reserve Bank to hold or even cut rates, one expert is bucking the trend and calling for rate hikes to tackle inflation. Markets are actually betting the RBA won't raise rates much more — which is one reason the Aussie dollar is rising even as rate-hike expectations fall. If this contrarian view gains traction, it could rattle bond and property markets.

stories.title: Aussie dollar rising despite fading RBA rate hike bets — here's why
stories.why_it_matters: Normally when a country's central bank is expected to keep rates low, its currency weakens. But the Aussie dollar is quietly climbing — likely because global investors are feeling more comfortable with risk assets and because commodity prices (outside of oil) are holding up. For you as an investor with USD-denominated holdings, a stronger AUD means those US assets are worth slightly less when converted back to Aussie dollars.

ai.summary: Today's AI headlines are dominated by two big themes: Google's launch of Gemini Omni — a powerful new AI model — and Pope Leo XIV publishing a major document calling for tight global regulation of AI and autonomous weapons. Thought-provoking stuff from both Silicon Valley and the Vatican.

stories.title: Google launches Gemini Omni — its most capable AI model yet
stories.why_it_matters: Google has announced Gemini Omni, described as its most capable AI model. 'Omni' typically means the model can handle text, images, audio, and video all in one — so it can see, hear, and read simultaneously. This is a direct shot at OpenAI's GPT-4o and signals Google is doubling down on its AI ambitions. Relevant for your GOOGL holding — Google is showing it's staying competitive at the frontier of AI development despite heavy competition.

stories.title: Pope Leo XIV calls for global AI regulation and warns autonomous weapons are ungovernable
stories.why_it_matters: Pope Leo XIV has released what's being described as a major manifesto on AI and humanity's future. He's calling for robust international regulation of artificial intelligence and specifically warned that autonomous weapons — drones or systems that can decide to kill without a human pressing a button — have already reached a point where they're impossible to effectively govern. The Pope is urging world governments to act before the technology outpaces all oversight. While this won't move markets directly, it reflects a growing global political pressure for AI regulation that could eventually affect the big tech companies you hold.

stories.title: Data privacy vs AI progress: the growing regulatory tension
stories.why_it_matters: A growing debate is playing out in regulatory circles: how do you protect people's personal data while also allowing AI companies to train their models on the vast amounts of data they need? Stricter privacy laws could slow down AI development, while looser rules risk misuse of personal information. This tension is particularly relevant for Alphabet (GOOGL) and Microsoft (MSFT), both of which rely heavily on data to power their AI products.

sport.summary: AFL fans are mourning the passing of Neale Daniher — one of the game's great figures. NRL Round 13 is shaping up with some big injury news affecting the Warriors and Tigers. And a World Surf League event in New Zealand was halted after an Australian photographer was bitten in a shark (or sea lion) incident.

stories.title: AFL legend Neale Daniher passes away — football world mourns
stories.why_it_matters: Neale Daniher — former Melbourne coach and one of the most beloved figures in Australian football — has passed away after a long battle with Motor Neurone Disease (MND). Daniher was diagnosed with MND in 2013 and became a tireless fundraiser for research through his 'Fight MND' charity, raising tens of millions of dollars. Garry Lyon and the AFL world have paid tribute, with Lyon calling on Prime Minister Albanese to honour Daniher's legacy. He leaves behind an enormous contribution both to football and to the MND community.

stories.title: NRL Round 13 injury news: Warriors and Tigers cop major blows
stories.why_it_matters: Heading into Round 13, the Warriors have been hit with a significant injury blow — Fox Sports reports one of their key players has confirmed he's done for the season, describing it as 'that's my footy done.' The Tigers are also without players ahead of their Saturday clash with the Bulldogs at Commbank Stadium. Mystery also surrounds which State of Origin stars will be available for club duty this round. Check the full team lists as they're confirmed Wednesday/Thursday.

stories.title: World Surf League event halted in NZ after Australian photographer bitten by shark (or sea lion)
stories.why_it_matters: A World Surf League competition in New Zealand was put on hold after an Australian photographer in the water was bitten by what is believed to be either a shark or a sea lion. The photographer was taken to hospital and the event was suspended while officials assessed the situation. No further details on the severity of injuries were available at the time of reporting.

stories.title: AFL's bye rounds under fire after Lions' big win exposed competition farce — Healy
stories.why_it_matters: Commentator Gerard Healy is calling out what he sees as the AFL's biggest structural problem: the scheduling of byes creating wildly uneven preparation time between clubs. He argues a blowout win by Brisbane highlights that when one team has a bye and the other doesn't, the competition loses credibility. AFL executives face one last chance this season to fix the draw, according to Healy.

watch_today.title: TTWO: Sharp drop — hold for now, but watch GTA 6 news closely
watch_today.detail: Take-Two fell nearly 4.5% last night to $227.55. There's no major single news catalyst — the GTA 6 collector's edition pre-order hype is building, but the stock has run hard in recent months. This could be profit-taking. If GTA 6 release date confirmation or a pricing announcement drops in the next few weeks, that's your next big catalyst either way. Sit tight for now.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX: Oil down 5% — energy ETF under pressure this week
watch_today.detail: Crude oil crashed nearly 5% last night to $91.79/barrel after OPEC cut its 2026 demand growth forecast. Your FUEL.AX energy ETF already slipped 0.9% today and could stay under pressure if oil keeps sliding. Nothing broken in the long-term thesis, but this is worth watching — if oil falls below $88-90, that's a meaningful headwind for this holding.

watch_today.title: Labor's CGT and negative gearing changes — property investors take note
watch_today.detail: If you hold investment properties or are planning to sell assets with large capital gains, Labor's proposed changes are worth understanding now. The CGT discount being cut from 50% to 25% would significantly increase the tax payable when you sell an investment. No legislation has passed yet, but the government is pushing ahead and ignoring calls to pause. Worth reviewing your tax position with your accountant.

watch_today.title: GOOGL: Gemini Omni launch is a positive signal — hold
watch_today.detail: Google dropped 1.2% last night despite launching Gemini Omni, its most capable AI model yet. The model can handle text, images, audio, and video simultaneously — keeping Google firmly in the AI race against OpenAI. The dip looks like routine market noise rather than anything fundamental. Recent earnings were strong. No reason to sell.

watch_today.title: Stronger AUD is a mild headwind for your US holdings
watch_today.detail: The Aussie dollar is nudging higher (now at 71.66 US cents) as rate-hike expectations soften. A stronger AUD means your USD-denominated holdings (GOOGL, MSFT, TTWO) are worth a little less when converted back to Aussie dollars. Nothing dramatic right now, but if the AUD keeps climbing toward 73-74 cents, it starts to bite more noticeably.
